phonePlan.note: The NANP (North American Numbering Plan) does not encode line type in the number itself: area codes and NXX blocks are assigned to carriers, not to service types, and Local Number Portability (LNP) lets any number move between mobile, landline and VoIP providers over time. As a result, no regex can reliably tell mobile from landline for Canadian numbers. Determining the actual line type requires querying a third-party line-type-intelligence service (e.g. Twilio Lookup, Neustar, IPQS) that cross-references the LERG (original block assignment) with the NPAC (Number Portability Administration Center, which tracks actual porting) for the current status, or performing a live HLR lookup to confirm an active mobile subscription (this only confirms mobile, not landline). Note: access to Canadian NPAC porting data typically requires separate approval from the lookup provider (e.g. Twilio requires a dedicated request for Canadian NPAC access). Implementation detail: trunkCode is intentionally left empty here (rather than "1") because it would be identical to dialCode and thus redundant; as a consequence, generic normalization helpers that strip dialCode then trunkCode will NOT automatically strip a leading "1" from an 11-digit domestic-format number (e.g. "12125550123"). Callers wanting to accept that common domestic format should strip a leading "1" explicitly for this country before testing against the regex.
